W3 (cost lens), after E029.

**Tip (E027).** E026 recipe at 8.75 true epochs: 219 steps at batch 2000, with the 20/24/28/32 px phases at 15/25/30/30% of steps. It measured 5.878 s at 0.7547 on seeds 0–2. I put the true mean at about 0.752–0.7535, so the tip sits on the bar. E029 (peak LR earlier) measured 0.7526 on seeds 0–2 with the same RNG stream, which fits a population mean near 0.753. There is no margin to spend.

**Time budget.** Time ≈ F + V × (pixel-weighted steps), with F ≈ 0.5 s.
- One step costs about 0.032 s at 32 px, 0.021 s at 24 px and 0.016 s at 20 px.
- Cutting 0.25 epoch saves about 0.14 s.
- My bias: I over-forecast time on 7 of the last 12 runs. Structural savings, such as removing high-res work or backward work, come in at about 1.5–4× my pixel/MAC model (E026, E028: −0.52 s against −0.12 s modelled). Correction: scale estimated savings by about 1.5 and shade forecasts low.
- Schedule-only changes (LR, LS, alpha) cost about 0 s (E029: −0.02 s).

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: about 1.5–2.5 s/pp.
- Early low-res phase: about 1+ s/pp (noisy).
- FreezeOut: about 0.5 s per 0.3 pp, so about 1.7 s/pp.
- No lever has beaten about 1.5 s/pp. The binding constraint is margin, not efficiency.

**Accuracy boosters: all flat.** LS (E013), Muon lr (E014), wd (E016/E022, inside noise), final LR (E009), alpha exponent (E025, −), warm-up (E029, −). Every remaining knob has a prior of about 0 ± 0.2 pp. Shifting the averaging or LR schedule has tended to hurt slightly: the airbench defaults sit near a local optimum.

**Mechanisms I believe:**
1. Lookahead endpoint averaging is worth about 1 pp (E005). A harder pull hurts (E025).
2. Muon is worth about +0.66 pp (E006). Filters are renormalized, so filter wd is inert.
3. Accuracy is built in the 28/32 px phases (E011, E018, E024). The earliest phase is cheap to degrade (E026).
4. Last-group width matters (E010).
5. RNG stream × seed effects are about ±0.3 pp on the 3-seed mean.

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp. The 10-seed held-out SE is about 0.1 pp.
- Time noise is about 1%.
- Any change to step count or data order re-rolls seeds 0–2.

**Unsure:**
- Loss-based example dropping: probably close to a uniform cut. Removing easy examples raises the effective LS and gradient noise.
- Per-resolution whitening: eigenvector sign and order are arbitrary, so unaligned bases jolt group 1 at every switch. Net effect is likely negative or zero.
- PCIe transfer of the margin.
- Whether any time-neutral booster exists at all. If none does, the only path is a cheaper lever that trades better than 1.5 s/pp, such as FreezeOut combined with something, or larger early-phase batches.

forecasts.reason: About 9% fewer steps saves about 0.35 s, but it costs about 0.3 pp like a uniform cut (easy examples still carry LS/averaging signal); no margin to absorb that.
Averaging-schedule knobs have been flat or negative (E025); a +0.15 pp held-out gain is unlikely. Fewer copies save a few ms.
LS changes were flat (E013). A late switch to sharp CE without smoothing tends to slightly hurt top-1 under EMA; expect about 0 ± 0.2 pp.
22 steps move from 24 to 20 px, about 0.15 s with my 1.5× correction. The early phase is cheap but not free: expect about −0.1 to −0.2 pp, which is borderline on the 0.15 pp bar.
Per-resolution eigenbases are unaligned (sign and order), so group 1 gets jolted at each switch; the stem mismatch is a minor cost next to the feature-map regime.

cruxes: Does any time-neutral change add at least 0.2 pp held-out? If none does, every time cut must trade better than about 1.5 s/pp, and only high-res/backward cuts (FreezeOut, 20 px phase) have come close.
What is the tip's true population mean (pooled seeds 3–22)? If it is at or below 0.752, the tip needs margin bought back before any further cut.
Does FreezeOut combined with a slightly longer 32 px tail, or batch 3000 in the low-res phases, trade better than 1.5 s/pp? Structural savings have come in 1.5–4× larger than modelled.
